name: attribute-invalid-unit-class
description: A schema unit class issue, saying there is an unknown one.
common_causes: Referencing non-existent unit classes in unitClass attributes
Using deprecated or removed unit classes
Missing unit class definitions in schema
explanation: UnitClass attributes must reference valid unit classes defined in the schema. Invalid unit class references cause validation failures and prevent proper unit validation.
correction_strategy: Use valid unit class names that exist in the schema

correction_examples.explanation: Replaced unknown unit class with valid one

correction_patterns: Verify unit class exists in schema
Check unit class name spelling and case
Use defined unit class names only
Remove references to non-existent unit classes
fix_instructions: 1. Check available unit classes in schema
validation_hints: Cross-reference with schema unit class definitions
Check unit class name case sensitivity
Verify unit class exists before referencing

name: attribute-invalid-multiple-unit-classes
description: A placeholder (#) lists more than one unit class in its unitClass attribute.
common_causes: Listing two unit classes on one placeholder to accept two kinds of units
Copying a unitClass attribute that was meant for a different placeholder
explanation: A # placeholder has at most one unit class (specification 4.0.0, section 3.1.4.4). Every unit in a class converts to that class's default unit, so one placeholder corresponds to one physical dimension, and a unit string is always checked against exactly one class.
correction_strategy: Keep one unit class per placeholder; use separate tags for values measured in different dimensions

correction_examples.explanation: Only one unit class may be listed

correction_patterns: Split a two-dimension quantity into two tags
fix_instructions: 1. Find every # placeholder that carries the unitClass attribute more than once
2. Decide which single unit class the placeholder should take
3. Move the other dimension to its own tag if it is still needed
validation_hints: In MediaWiki a repeated attribute is written unitClass=a, unitClass=b; loaders join the values with a comma, and more than one value is an error
The check applies to every schema version; no released schema has such a placeholder

name: attribute-invalid-unit-class-without-numeric-value-class
description: A placeholder (#) has a unitClass attribute but its valueClass is not numericClass, or it has no valueClass.
common_causes: Giving a text-valued placeholder a unit class so that units can follow the text
Forgetting the valueClass attribute on a placeholder that takes a unit class
explanation: A value with units is a number that is converted to the default units of its unit class, so a # placeholder with a unit class must have valueClass=numericClass (specification 4.0.0, section 3.1.4.4). The rule applies to standard schemas 8.5.0 and later and to libraries partnered with them; 8.3.0 and earlier have Sampling-rate/# with a unit class and no value class.
correction_strategy: Add valueClass=numericClass to the placeholder, or remove the unit class if the value is not a number

correction_examples.explanation: A unit class needs a numeric value
The value class must be stated

correction_patterns: Text values do not take unit classes
fix_instructions: 1. Find every # placeholder with a unitClass attribute
2. Check that its valueClass attribute is exactly numericClass
3. Add or correct the valueClass, or drop the unitClass for non-numeric values
validation_hints: Check only schemas whose standard version (own or withStandard) is 8.5.0 or later; unpartnered libraries are not checked
A missing valueClass counts as a violation
